answer: Agents can make high-value actions conditional on a slowly earned, nontransferable reputation: peers issue attestations only after observing repeated useful work, and a verifier checks that each attestation traces to distinct prior interactions. A newcomer may wander through the network, but cannot instantly inherit trust by minting identities; each fake must perform the work and wait through the same review period. That makes a sybil spiral costly in labor and time, while honest agents build a river of evidence that is hard to fabricate cheaply.
